text.content:
Combat is simply Physical Challenges used to harm an opponent, layered with a few extra rules for movement, surprise, and gear.

Movement and Surprise

  • Three Step Rule: A combatant may take up to three steps while still attacking. One step is cautious movement, two steps (moving directly) costs a Trait down in the challenge, and three steps (running) also costs a Trait down.
  • Surprise: If a player doesn't respond within three seconds of a challenge being declared, she is surprised: the first exchange can only harm her, not the attacker. A surprised loser may call a second challenge by risking another Trait; afterward, normal rules resume.
  • Fair Escape: A character may call "Fair Escape!" to leave an area without pursuit when another player approaches, provided the approaching player isn't already within conversational distance, the character isn't ambushed/surrounded, and ranged weapons aren't already trained on her. Supernatural speed (e.g., Celerity) can grant or deny a Fair Escape depending on who has the higher level active.

Weapons

No real or prop weapons are used at the table; weapon cards represent each item's Traits. A weapon grants bonus Traits added to a wielder's total in relevant challenges (not usable as an initial bid), may carry a Negative Trait usable against its wielder, and has a concealability rating and an availability/cost tier.

Special Weapon Capabilities

  • Armor-Piercing — ignores armor's protective health levels.
  • Destroy Shield — automatically disables a shield after a set number of hits.
  • Fully Automatic — inflicts an extra health level from sustained fire, but requires a reload afterward.
  • High-Caliber — a Simple Test on a successful hit adds an extra health level of damage.
  • Incendiary — inflicts aggravated damage, as fire does to vampires.
  • Mass-Trauma — scores an extra health level of damage outright.
  • Speed — lets a Melee-trained wielder pre-empt and strike first against clumsy, heavy, or slow weapons.
  • Spray — one test can strike several adjacent targets at once.
  • Staking — a piercing weapon that lands a hit can attempt to stake a vampire's heart by winning or tying two successive Simple Tests, paralyzing the target.

Bidding Weapon Traits

Hand-to-hand combat bids Physical Traits. A character firing a gun bids Mental Traits instead; if her opponent is unarmed and merely dodging, the defender still uses Physical Traits to resist.

Example Melee Weapons

  • Knife/Dagger: 2 bonus Traits, Negative Trait Short, conceals in a pocket, one health level of damage, Speed special ability.
  • Wooden Stake: 2 bonus Traits, Negative Trait Short, one health level of damage, Staking special ability.
  • Club/Axe: Club 2 / Axe 3 bonus Traits, Negative Trait Clumsy, one (club) or two (axe) health levels of damage; axes can Destroy Shield.
  • Fencing Blade: 2 bonus Traits, Negative Trait Fragile, one health level of damage, Speed special ability.
  • Longbow: 6 bonus Traits (5 for a compound bow, which loses Clumsy), Negative Traits Fragile/Clumsy/Heavy, two health levels of damage, Armor-Piercing, Staking, and Destroy Shield.

Example Firearms

  • Pistol: 2 bonus Traits, Negative Trait Loud, two health levels of damage.
  • Heavy Pistol: 2 bonus Traits, Negative Trait Loud, two health levels of damage, High-Caliber.
  • Rifle: 3 bonus Traits, Negative Trait Loud, two health levels of damage, can be loaded for High-Caliber.
  • Shotgun: 3 bonus Traits, Negative Trait Loud, two health levels of damage, Spray (pellet loads) and Mass-Trauma (close range).
  • Submachine Gun: 2 bonus Traits, Negative Trait Loud, two health levels of damage, Spray and (if converted) Fully Automatic.

Armor

Armor grants extra health levels that absorb damage before the wearer is harmed, but does nothing against non-physical attacks like blood-boiling Thaumaturgy. Chain-mail (2 levels, Heavy) and plate mail (3 levels, Heavy/Clumsy) are rare antiques; ballistic vests (2 levels, Heavy) and reinforced vests (3 levels, Heavy/Clumsy) are the modern equivalents, generally available only through Police or Underworld Influence.

Ranged Combat and Cover

A ranged attacker must still approach and declare the shot before testing. A target unaware of the attack (or without a ranged weapon of his own) is treated as surprised for as long as the aggressor keeps winning. Combatants may each claim cover Traits (added to totals, not bid directly) representing available obstacles; total concealment makes a target impossible to hit until the attacker repositions.

Melee and Brawling

Melee requires weapon's-reach distance; brawling requires arm's-length distance. Absent a special power, all brawling damage is one health level of bashing damage regardless of the roleplayed description. A specialized fighting style (bought under Melee or Brawl) grants flavor and retests but not extra damage.

Two-Weapon Fighting

Using the off-hand imposes a two-Trait penalty (so three Traits must be bid in total) unless the character has the Ambidextrous Merit, which removes the off-hand penalty (though using both hands at once still costs two Traits per hand). A Two-Weapon Combat or Florentine specialization removes one penalty Trait from off-hand use. Using both hands grants only one extra action regardless of Celerity-style bonus actions, split evenly between the hands.

Contests of Will

A staring contest between two characters intended to force a backdown is best roleplayed directly; if neither relents, a Social Challenge decides the winner, with the loser breaking eye contact.
